youtube.title: TWO BLOKES & A BOT
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide and software developer Tauriq Barron explore how rapidly AI is reshaping work, education and everyday life, questioning whether politicians and institutions are keeping pace. They discuss AI’s impact on software developers, the lack of coherent political policy on AI in education, and proposed regulation that could entrench the biggest technology companies. Rodney also reflects on using AI for unexpectedly rich theological conversations. youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: With the 2026 election just four weeks away, Paul Brennan speaks with New Zealand First leader and Foreign Minister Winston Peters about the latest polling, media coverage, immigration-system failures and concerns over digital ID. Peters also discusses the need for economic growth, a further Covid inquiry and his party’s remaining campaign policies, arguing that New Zealand needs greater ambition and a clearer path to recovery. youtube.title: DR ERIC CRAMPTON
youtube.summary: With the election looming, New Zealand Initiative chief economist Eric Crampton joins Paul Brennan to assess an EU complaint over New Zealand’s environmental policies, Labour’s proposed student loan write-offs and National’s plan to break up the major supermarkets. Crampton argues the trade complaint poses little immediate risk, while questioning the economic logic of loan write-offs and warning that supermarket reform should tackle regulatory barriers and property-rights concerns first. For more from Dr Eric Crampton, head to NZ Initiative For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: PAUL HOPKINSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Paul Hopkinson, founder and leader of the newly registered Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party, about the party’s aims and its decision to contest the election. Hopkinson outlines his views on Palestine, New Zealand’s foreign policy, Five Eyes, military alliances and armed resistance, while also discussing his activism, arrests and the party’s broadcasting allocation. He says the party’s primary goal is building a movement rather than winning seats. For more information visit the Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: DR DAVID WILSON
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Dr David Wilson, NZ First List MP for Auckland, about Auckland’s economic challenges, infrastructure and CBD decline, before examining New Zealand First’s small-business policies and plans to reduce tax and borrowing costs. They discuss BNZ ownership, KiwiSaver, digital privacy, AI regulation and data sovereignty, with Wilson outlining his party’s approach to balancing technological opportunity with safeguards for individual autonomy. youtube.title: DAVID MAYWALD
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with David Maywald, chair of the International Council for Men and Boys, about the widening gaps facing boys and young men in education, health funding and public empathy. David explains the concept of gynocentrism, pointing to disparities in medical research funding and domestic violence services and argues that resilience, mentorship, and faith are essential to helping young men find purpose and belonging. youtube.title: CYNTHIA HANCOX
youtube.summary: Simon O'Connor and Cynthia Hancox discuss proposed changes to home education, following recent reviews and concerns raised around homeschooling in New Zealand. They explore balancing child safety with family choice, current review processes and the need for practical consultation between home educators and the Ministry of Education. She tackled tough questions about economic impact, farmer livelihoods, and even diesel shortages threatening animal welfare — making a compelling case that short-sighted thinking is the real economic danger. youtube.title: SAL MERCOGLIANO
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with maritime historian Dr Sal Mercogliano about the ongoing disruption to global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, now seven months into the conflict. Sal explains why refined fuel exports remain far below pre-war levels despite crude flows recovering, breaks down the soaring cost of tanker charters and war risk insurance and discusses the covert use of armed escort ships like the St Helena, before warning that full normalisation could take at least a year and urging New Zealand to reconsider a national shipping line. Discover more from Sal on X and his YouTube channel | What's Going On With Shipping? For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: TAINE RANDALL
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with Taine Randell, NZ First candidate for the Tukituki electorate about his decision to leave a long business and rugby career for politics. He discusses breaking up energy companies, banks and supermarkets, his frustration over Fonterra selling off iconic dairy brands, the toll high energy costs have taken on Hawke's Bay manufacturing, and why he believes New Zealand needs to rediscover its entrepreneurial edge.
